doc.title: Mike Vax interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 29, 2022

title: Stan Kenton as a hands-on leader
summary: Kenton demanded full concentration, and once ordered everyone to read every chart; he was like a father.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: A number of Basie alums have talked about how the Count was sort of a hands off — he didn’t say anything unless something was really bad. And I wondered if Stan was like that or was he more hands-on and how did he deal with any, I guess I’ll call them discipline issues?

Well first of all Stan was very hands-on. And to play in that band you had to be 110% all the time. You know, the concentration level — I’ll tell you — this is a great one. I don’t remember when this happened but it was something where, you know any of the band leaders, they’re basically going to play tunes from the last album and tunes that made them famous. And so they get into this thing of different tours you’re going to play almost the same charts every night. You know. And sometimes the band is getting oooo — let’s do something different. And this one time I remember Stan had been thinking © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

about it and as I said he was very hands-on. And so before this one concert he came in front of the band and he said, “The band is getting complacent and I don’t like it.” He said, “You guys aren’t getting your charts up.” You know you get to the point where you’ve got the charts memorized you know? You’ve got the order memorized and you’ve got the charts memorized. So he said, “Every person will get out every chart and read every note tonight.” And you know what? The band sounded different. You know and so I would say he was very hands-on but you’ve got to remember almost everybody that ever played on that band said he was the best leader to work for. You know he was like a father to us. You know they called him the old man in the earlier bands, even though he wasn’t that much older than them, but yeah he was — you had to be there. You had to be on top of things all the time and I can remember times when he wasn’t happy with some people and he’d call them aside and say, “Hey man, you’ve got to be doing better.” And it wasn’t — it was never mean. It never felt like he was being mean. It felt like he was being the father figure, you know, taking care of the business of the band.
